problem.statement: WPF's native DataGrid becomes drastically slower than the old Silverlight grid when filtering, because a CollectionView Reset event triggers a deeply nested recursive DescendantsWalker/UpdateLayout cycle that developers can profile but not fix.

persona.primary: WPF developer migrating a large custom-grid Silverlight application to WPF

context.situation: A team porting a Silverlight app with a custom DataGrid used across nearly all views finds filtering takes ~5x longer in WPF (3.7s vs 700ms) and their own profiling only reveals the call tree, not a solution.

current_workarounds: Built parallel Silverlight and WPF test apps with identical data to isolate and compare the performance gap
Used the dotTrace profiler to capture call-tree snapshots of the filtering/layout operations to locate the bottleneck
existing_substitutes: dotTrace (used for profiling, not as a fix)

possible_wedges.offer: Fixed-price diagnostic engagement: send us your DataGrid/filtering setup and profiler trace, we identify the specific WPF layout/virtualization anti-pattern and deliver a working fix or mitigation.

Standalone analyzer that ingests a WPF app's XAML/bindings (or a dotTrace/PerfView snapshot) and flags known DataGrid/ItemsControl performance anti-patterns like CollectionChanged.Reset triggering full UpdateLayout, with suggested remediations.
Command-line audit that scans a WPF/.NET codebase for legacy performance and binding anti-patterns inherited from Silverlight ports, producing a report ranked by expected impact.

risks: Single evidence item from one forum thread — no confirmation this is a widespread, recurring pain point
Signals show low commercial intent and commitment (0.15 and 0.1), suggesting the poster wants a free community answer, not a paid fix
The underlying issue may require a genuine WPF framework-level workaround (custom ItemsControl/virtualization) rather than something auditable or automatable
No named competing tools or substitutes appear in the evidence, so it's unclear whether buyers would look for a paid solution at all versus continuing to search forums for free
Only one persona type (Silverlight-to-WPF migration developer) represented; unclear how common this specific migration scenario still is in 2026

cheapest_experiment.hypothesis: WPF developers hitting this specific DataGrid filtering slowdown would pay for a fixed-price diagnostic that pinpoints the cause and supplies a working fix, rather than continuing to self-profile with no resolution.
cheapest_experiment.input: Reply to this and similar unanswered WPF performance threads (Stack Overflow, MSDN/Microsoft Q&A, relevant subreddits) offering a paid fixed-price diagnosis-and-fix for DataGrid/CollectionView Reset performance issues, linking to a simple booking/payment page.
cheapest_experiment.output: Count of thread engagements, DMs, and payment-page visits/starts generated from the outreach.
cheapest_experiment.commitment_event: At least one developer pays the fixed fee (or puts down a deposit) for the diagnostic engagement.
cheapest_experiment.success_threshold: 3+ people from outreach express concrete willingness to pay or start checkout within 2-3 weeks
cheapest_experiment.failure_threshold: 0-1 people engage with willingness to pay after posting in several relevant threads
